subject: religious-studies
topicDisplay: Islam Beliefs Crime Punishment Living The Muslim Life Peace Conflict Spec A
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: Tawhid, the most important belief in Islam, means:
questions.explain: Tawhid is the belief in the absolute oneness and unity of God (Allah).

questions.q: Which of the following is a condition of Just War theory?
options: The war must aim to destroy as many people as possible
The war must be started for personal profit
The war must be a last resort with a just cause
questions.explain: Just War theory requires a just cause, proper authority, last resort and proportionate, discriminating force.

questions.q: A common misconception about pacifism is that:
options: Pacifists must be passive and do nothing about injustice
Many pacifists actively work for peace through non-violent means
questions.explain: Many pacifists are very active, using non-violent protest and campaigning rather than doing nothing.

questions.explain: Risalah is the belief in prophethood, that God sent prophets and messengers to guide humanity.
Akhirah is the belief in life after death and an eternal existence beyond this life.

questions.q: The five roots of Usul ad-Din are the foundations of faith for:
questions.explain: The five roots of Usul ad-Din are the key beliefs that form the foundation of Shia Islam.

questions.q: The main cause of the Sunni-Shia split was disagreement over:
options: Who should lead the Muslim community after Muhammad's death
questions.explain: The split arose over who should be the rightful leader of Muslims after Muhammad died.

questions.q: What is the difference between 'prison' and 'rehabilitation'?
options: Prison removes freedom; rehabilitation tries to help offenders change
Prison aims only to reward offenders
questions.explain: Prison restricts liberty, while rehabilitation focuses on changing behaviour and reintegrating offenders.

questions.q: For Muslims, the Qur'an is believed to be:
options: A book written after his death by historians
The direct word of God revealed to Muhammad
questions.explain: Muslims believe the Qur'an is the literal word of God revealed to the Prophet Muhammad.

questions.q: The angel who revealed the Qur'an to Muhammad is named:
questions.explain: The angel Jibril (Gabriel) revealed the Qur'an to the Prophet Muhammad.

questions.q: In Islam, Muhammad is regarded as:
options: The final prophet (the Seal of the Prophets)
questions.explain: Muslims believe Muhammad is the last and final prophet, the Seal of the Prophets.

questions.q: Which is commonly listed as a cause of war?
options: Greed, ideology and the desire for power or land
questions.explain: Common causes of war include greed, self-defence, ideology and competition for resources.
